label: D1 reward-seen after unrewarded trials, late episode, policy toward a1, scaled by episode time
explanation: Fires only at D1, and only when the previous trial was rewarded; zero at GO and D2. Within D1 its size follows the episode-time profile (near zero before trial 30, rising to a peak around trials 60-89, lower in the last decile), and every term is multiplicative with that profile. Unrewarded D1 steps sit at about zero, so a term cancels the timing baseline there. On rewarded D1 steps it is larger when the trial before was unrewarded (and larger again if the trial two back was also unrewarded): a reward after a dry spell gives about 0.5-0.9, a reward after a reward much less. It also grows with the a1-leaning part of the policy logit (max(choice,0)) and is higher when the rewarded state was S2. Value adds nothing. All terms are observed or model-internal; none is future. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.57, test 0.51. The additive all ceiling is 0.23, which the multiplicative episode-time interaction exceeds.

issues: The core claims hold. The profile shows the feature is zero at GO and D2. It is about zero on unrewarded D1 steps, its D1 baseline follows the claimed episode-decile profile, and a reward after a dry spell raises it. Adding the reward-two-back term to rewarded x episode-profile takes test R^2 from 0.05 to 0.17, and the reward-three-back term gets weight +0.115. The reported 0.507 test R^2 reproduces exactly.

The 'a1-leaning policy' effect is convex and the stated terms only fit it linearly. Adding R*max(choice,0)^2 to [R, R*(r-2==0), R*max(choice,0)] raises test R^2 from 0.42 to 0.51. Once the squared term is in, the linear max(choice,0) weight turns negative (-0.06 to -0.10), so the effect is concentrated in strong a1-leaning policies.

The claim 'slightly higher when the rewarded state was S2' gets the transition structure wrong. Splitting rewarded D1 steps by the previous trial's choice x state gives a1 S2 r (rare rewarded after a1) +0.09 to +0.13, a1 S1 r -0.05 to -0.07, a2 S1 r -0.12 and a2 S2 r about 0 (reference). The big effect is rare-rewarded after a1 (a model-based 'switch to a2' trial), with a1 S1 r and a2 S1 r below the reference, not a mild S2 bonus.

Misses on the original terms show systematic errors by previous trial at D1. Steps after a2 S1 r are over-predicted (-0.020) and steps after a1 S2 r are under-predicted (+0.012). The worst windows are activations of 0.65-0.86 predicted at only 0.04-0.25, mostly rewarded trials that reached S2 (often rare from a1). After adding the choice-x-state table and the squared choice term, the largest per-cell error drops to about 0.010.

A future variable is strongly linked to the feature. With [R, R*(r-2==0), max(choice,0), max(choice,0)^2] in the fit, adding the upcoming choice (action==2) gets weight +0.23 and raises test R^2 from 0.51 to 0.53. The observed-only stand-in (the previous trial's choice x state, a1 S2 r) does about as well: test 0.53 with the a1 S2 r / a2 S2 r / a1 S1 r split in place of action==2. This fits a 'reward says switch to a2' signal, which the label's 'a1-leaning policy' framing hides.

Observed-only better terms reach test R^2 0.606 (dev 0.639), against 0.507 for the reported terms. The label is not wrong, but it leaves out structure worth about 0.10 R^2 and mis-describes the state effect.

Larger after a dry spell, larger the more strongly (convexly) the policy leans a1, and largest when the reward came via a rare a1->S2 transition (a model-based 'switch to a2' trial). Lower after a1 S1 r and a2 S1 r. Zero at GO and D2.
